events.excerpt: The once-multi-billion-dollar insurance company Goosehead lost one-fifth of its market capitalization in the past week after an SEC comment letter prompted it to retract and restate three years of financials. Year-to-date, shareholders have lost one-third of their investment. On a trendline toward becoming a billion-dollar company — if not smaller — the NASDAQ-listed policy broker admitted that audited financial statements for 2023, 2024, 2025, and every quarter through June 2026 are unreliable. It also warned that its report for the third quarter of 2026 will be arriving late and that its investor day is postponed. The company expects to report material weaknesses in how it maintained its own books. Goosehead expensed certain commissions paid to its corporate sales agents up-front instead of deferring part of them. It also netted fees collected from franchisees against expenses, instead of booking them as revenue, which mis-stated 2025 revenue. CEO Mark Miller tried to spin things positively, “These adjustments have no impact on our cash flows or business operations.” Shareholders weren’t entirely convinced, however, selling down its common stock by nearly 16% on Tuesday alone. events.excerpt: I would like to discuss a wallet design built around three components: Lindell 2-of-2 MPC signing, QR-only initialization, and encrypted NFC communication between a computer and a phone. The goal is to keep the convenience of a desktop wallet while ensuring that compromising either device alone does not provide unilateral signing authority. Lindell 2-of-2 MPC as the signing foundation The computer and phone each hold a private share of one joint signing key. Neither device holds the complete private key. Using a reviewed implementation of Lindell’s two-party ECDSA protocol , both devices interact to compute a signature without revealing their shares or reconstructing the complete private key. For Ethereum, the implementation would use secp256k1 and produce one ordinary ECDSA signature under the joint public key. The wallet can therefore use a normal Ethereum address without requiring an on-chain multisignature contract. The 2-of-2 requirement comes from the signing protocol itself: obtaining the computer’s share alone is insufficient, and obtaining the phone’s share alone is also insufficient. Both devices must participate in signing the same transaction. Initialize entirely through QR codes Initialization takes place before connecting the NFC reader. Each device generates its ow

events.excerpt: title: [Direct-to-AIP] Reserve Factor Updates Across Aave V3 and V2 Markets author: @TokenLogic created: 2026-11-12 Summary This publication proposes Reserve Factor updates on 54 reserves across 12 Aave V3 instances and the Aave V2 Ethereum market. At balances and rates as of 9 November 2026, the changes add about $3.5M of annualised revenue to the DAO and raise the blended RF from 12.0% to 12.7%. The proposal is part of the ongoing effort to streamline Aave V3. Motivation Overview Over the past months, the DAO has been streamlining Aave V3. Low-adoption reserves and instances have been wound down, Aave V2 has been frozen, and ongoing work aims to focus Ethereum Core on liquid, bluechip collateral, with assets that carry additional risk moving to Aave V4, where that risk can be priced. This proposal applies the same direction to the protocol’s revenue side. Every borrowable reserve exposes the DAO to collateral, oracle and liquidation risk. The RF compensates the DAO for carrying that risk. On many reserves today, the DAO keeps a small share of the interest on positions whose tail risk it fully underwrites. Raising the RF improves the DAO’s return for the same risk, without changing the rate any borrower pays. On legacy markets, it also lowers the incentive to keep liquidity wher
